narrative:
The model estimates there’s a 40% chance you won’t pass your final year, which is well above the 10% threshold that requires extra support. Because of this, you’ll need to take remedial courses to help you stay on track.

The main reasons the model is concerned come down to three key areas. First, you’ve never failed a class before, which actually works in your favor—it shows you have the ability to keep up when things are going smoothly. However, the other two factors are pulling the prediction the other way. Your parents both left school after primary education, and students whose parents have less formal schooling tend to face more challenges in their final year. This doesn’t mean you can’t succeed, but it does suggest you might need additional strategies to bridge any gaps in support at home.

The model also noticed that your family relationships are rated as very bad, which is quite rare among students who pass. When family life is stressful, it can make it harder to focus on schoolwork, even if you’re putting in study time. The good news is that these are areas where targeted help—like the remedial courses—can make a real difference.

Next steps are clear: attend the remedial sessions, use the extra study time to strengthen weak subjects, and consider talking to a counselor about ways to improve your home environment. Small changes in these areas could significantly lower the risk of struggling at the end of the year.
